title: UPSC CSE — CSAT Aptitude | Logical Deduction
description: Subject-wise test on Logical Deduction (CSAT Aptitude) for UPSC CSE. 27Q.
subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: Based on the passage, which of the following statements can be logically deduced?

options.text: Eating whole grains and fresh vegetables guarantees immunity from heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that whole grains and fresh vegetables guarantee immunity.

options.text: Individuals who do not consume whole grains and fresh vegetables will definitely develop chronic diseases.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that not consuming whole grains and fresh vegetables guarantees the development of chronic diseases.

options.text: A diet rich in whole grains and fresh vegetables is associated with a reduced risk of certain chronic diseases.
options.explanation: The passage states that individuals who regularly consume a diet rich in whole grains and fresh vegetables tend to have lower incidences of chronic diseases.

options.text: Chronic diseases are solely caused by dietary deficiencies in whole grains and fresh vegetables.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that chronic diseases are solely caused by dietary deficiencies in whole grains and fresh vegetables.

questions.explanation: The passage states a correlation and lower incidences, indicating an association or reduced risk, not a guarantee of immunity or certainty of developing diseases.
questions.subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid inference from the passage regarding the proposed solution?

options.text: Investing in public transportation will completely eliminate traffic congestion and carbon emissions.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that investing in public transportation will completely eliminate traffic congestion and carbon emissions.

options.text: The success of public transportation investment depends on commuters choosing it over private vehicles.
options.explanation: The passage implies that the effectiveness of the solution relies on commuters actually making the choice to use public transportation.

options.text: Public transportation is inherently more environmentally friendly than private vehicles.
options.explanation: The passage does not make a general claim about the environmental friendliness of public transportation compared to private vehicles.

options.text: All cities currently lack efficient, accessible, and affordable public transportation networks.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that all cities lack efficient, accessible, and affordable public transportation networks.

questions.explanation: The passage states that investment in public transportation would encourage more commuters to leave their private vehicles at home, implying that the success of the solution relies on commuters making that choice.
questions.subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: Suppose Country X is currently experiencing a prolonged period of high inflation. Which of the following is the most logical consequence for Country X, based on the passage?

options.text: Its domestic industries that rely on imports will likely thrive.
options.explanation: The passage implies that imports become more expensive, which would not help domestic industries that rely on imports.

options.text: Its currency is expected to appreciate against major foreign currencies.
options.explanation: The passage states that high inflation tends to depreciate a country's currency.

options.text: The cost of imported goods for Country X will likely increase.
options.explanation: The passage states that a depreciated currency makes imports more expensive.

options.text: Its export-oriented industries will definitely decline.
options.explanation: The passage suggests that exports become cheaper, potentially boosting export-oriented industries.

questions.explanation: The passage states that a depreciated currency makes imports more expensive, and since Country X is experiencing high inflation, its currency would depreciate.
questions.subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a direct inference from the passage?

options.text: The brain's energy consumption varies significantly during different activities.
options.explanation: The passage states that the brain's high energy demand is constant.

options.text: The brain is the most energy-intensive organ in the human body relative to its size.
options.explanation: The passage states that the brain consumes a disproportionately large amount of the body's total energy despite accounting for only a small percentage of the body's weight.

options.text: Sleep requires less brain energy than being awake.
options.explanation: The passage states that the brain's high energy demand is constant, even during sleep.

options.text: The brain is the heaviest organ in the human body.
options.explanation: The passage states that the brain accounts for only about 2% of the body's weight.

questions.explanation: The passage states that all mammals have hair and that Fido is a mammal, so Fido must have hair.

questions.question: Which of the following assumptions is implicit in the critics' argument?

options.text: Solar panels are an ineffective means of reducing carbon footprint.
options.explanation: The critics' argument is about the cost, not the effectiveness of solar panels.

options.text: The cost of installing solar panels will be passed on to homebuyers.
options.explanation: The critics' argument implies that the cost of solar panels will increase housing costs for homebuyers.

options.text: Low-income families do not care about reducing carbon footprint.
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that low-income families do not care about reducing carbon footprint.

options.text: There are no government subsidies available for solar panel installation.
options.explanation: The passage does not mention government subsidies as a factor in the critics' argument.

questions.explanation: The critics argue that the policy will increase housing costs, implying that the cost of solar panels will be passed on to homebuyers.

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions can be most logically drawn from the passage?

options.text: Strong social cohesion is the primary cause of low crime rates in communities.
options.explanation: The passage notes that the direction of causality is uncertain.

options.text: Low crime rates are a direct result of increased participation in local events.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim a direct causal relationship between participation in local events and low crime rates.

options.text: There is a correlation between social cohesion and crime rates, but the direction of causality is uncertain.
options.explanation: The passage states a correlation between social cohesion and crime rates but notes that it is unclear whether strong social cohesion directly deters crime or if communities with lower crime rates develop stronger social bonds.

options.text: Socioeconomic factors are irrelevant in determining crime rates when social cohesion is high.
options.explanation: The passage controls for socioeconomic factors but does not claim they are irrelevant.

questions.explanation: The passage states a correlation between social cohesion and crime rates but notes that the direction of causality is uncertain.

questions.question: Which of the following statements must be true?

options.text: Fido is a carnivore.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about Fido's diet.

options.text: Fido has hair.
options.explanation: The passage states that all mammals have hair, and Fido is a mammal.

options.text: All carnivores are mammals.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about the classification of carnivores.

options.text: Some mammals are not carnivores.
options.explanation: While this statement may be true, it cannot be directly deduced from the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage states that all mammals have hair and that Fido is a mammal, so Fido must have hair.

questions.question: Which of the following situations, if true, would most strongly contradict the idea presented in the passage?

options.text: A highly diverse ecosystem collapses after a major environmental change.
options.explanation: This situation does not necessarily contradict the idea that higher biodiversity is associated with greater resilience.

options.text: An ecosystem with low biodiversity proves to be very stable over decades.
options.explanation: This situation directly contradicts the passage's claim that higher biodiversity is associated with greater resilience.

options.text: A species-rich forest experiences a minor pest outbreak with no lasting damage.
options.explanation: This situation supports the passage's claim that higher biodiversity is associated with greater resilience.

options.text: Scientists discover a new species in a previously unstudied rainforest.
options.explanation: This situation is unrelated to the idea presented in the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage argues that higher biodiversity is associated with greater resilience, but an ecosystem with low biodiversity being very stable would contradict this idea.

questions.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred about the future of employment based on the passage?

options.text: AI will only create new jobs without displacing any existing ones.
options.explanation: The passage mentions that AI could automate many existing jobs, leading to job displacement.

options.text: The total number of jobs in the economy will necessarily decrease due to AI.
options.explanation: The passage does not provide information about the net effect of AI on the total number of jobs.

options.text: Employment patterns are likely to undergo significant structural changes due to AI.
options.explanation: The passage mentions both job creation and job displacement, implying significant changes in the types and distribution of jobs.

options.text: AI will primarily impact high-skilled jobs, leaving low-skilled jobs untouched.
options.explanation: The passage mentions that AI could automate many existing jobs, particularly those with routine tasks, which are often low-skilled.

questions.explanation: The passage mentions both job creation and job displacement due to AI, implying significant structural changes in employment patterns.

questions.question: Which of the following statements represents the most accurate and comprehensive deduction from the passage?

options.text: Green spaces are the sole determinant of resident satisfaction and heat-related illness prevention in cities.
options.explanation: The passage does not claim that green spaces are the sole determinant of these benefits.

options.text: The presence of green spaces in urban areas offers health and well-being benefits, despite implementation hurdles.
options.explanation: The passage states that green spaces are associated with higher resident satisfaction and lower instances of heat-related illnesses, while also acknowledging challenges related to land availability and development costs.

options.text: Cities should prioritize green infrastructure over all other forms of urban development.
options.explanation: The passage does not make a prescriptive claim about prioritizing green infrastructure over other forms of development.

options.text: High population density and low average income prevent cities from developing green spaces.
options.explanation: The passage mentions these as challenges but does not claim they are absolute barriers to developing green spaces.

questions.explanation: The passage states that green spaces offer health and well-being benefits but also acknowledges implementation challenges.

questions.question: Based on the given statements, which of the following must be true?

options.text: All animals with wings are birds.
options.explanation: The ability to fly or having wings is not exclusive to birds.

options.text: Some animals with feathers cannot fly.
options.explanation: There are birds that do not fly, and all birds have feathers.

options.text: All birds can fly.
options.explanation: This contradicts the statement 'Some birds can fly.'

options.text: All animals that can fly are birds.
options.explanation: The ability to fly is not exclusive to birds.

questions.explanation: We know 'All birds have feathers' and 'Some birds can fly.' This implies that there are birds that do not fly (because only some can). Since all birds have feathers, it logically follows that some animals with feathers (specifically, the birds that cannot fly) cannot fly.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most direct conclusion from the passage?

options.text: Expanding public transportation will always lead to a decrease in private vehicle ownership.
options.explanation: This is a definitive cause-and-effect statement not directly supported by the passage.

options.text: People prefer public transportation over private vehicles when given the option.
options.explanation: This is a universal preference not directly stated in the passage.

options.text: There is a correlation between robust public transport and reduced private vehicle ownership.
options.explanation: The passage points directly to a correlation or link between public transport and private vehicle ownership.

options.text: Cities should ban private vehicles to promote public transport usage.
options.explanation: This is a policy recommendation not supported by the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the survey 'indicated that cities with extensive public transportation networks have lower rates of private vehicle ownership' and that this 'suggests that the availability of efficient public transport can influence urban commuting choices.'

options.text: Humanities courses are becoming irrelevant in the modern job market.

This trend is often attributed to the perceived higher earning potential in STEM careers.'

questions.question: Which of the following can be logically deduced from the statement above?

options.text: Ramesh has voted in an election.
options.explanation: The statement does not mention Ramesh voting in an election, only that he is eligible to vote.

questions.question: Consider the following argument: Premise 1: All mangoes are fruits. Premise 2: This item is a fruit. Conclusion: Therefore, this item is a mango. Which of the following statements most accurately assesses the logical validity of the conclusion?

options.text: The conclusion is logically valid because the item fits the description of a fruit.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because being a fruit does not necessarily mean the item is a mango.

options.text: The conclusion is logically invalid because being a fruit does not exclusively mean the item must be a mango.
options.explanation: This option is correct because it identifies the argument as logically invalid due to the fact that being a fruit is a characteristic of many items, not just mangoes.

options.text: The conclusion is valid only if the item has the taste of a mango.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because the taste of the item is not relevant to the logical validity of the conclusion based on the given premises.

options.text: The conclusion is invalid because the premises do not explicitly state what the item is.
options.explanation: While this statement about the premises not explicitly stating what the item is might seem relevant, it does not directly address the logical validity of the conclusion based on the information given.

questions.explanation: This is an example of an invalid deductive argument, specifically an example of affirming the consequent.

questions.question: Which of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?

options.text: Economic development is inherently incompatible with environmental conservation.
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that economic development is inherently incompatible with environmental conservation, but rather that current policies often prioritize short-term economic gains over ecological preservation.

options.text: The negative environmental impacts of mining are primarily due to a lack of advanced technology.
options.explanation: The passage does not mention a lack of advanced technology as the primary cause of the negative environmental impacts of mining.

options.text: Current policies often prioritize short-term economic gains over ecological preservation.
options.explanation: The passage states that current policies frequently prioritize short-term economic gains over ecological preservation, which is a logical inference from the passage.

options.text: Sustainable development is not possible in regions with significant mineral resources.
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that sustainable development is not possible in regions with significant mineral resources, but rather that it mandates a balance between economic development and ecological preservation.

questions.explanation: The passage discusses the trade-off between economic development and environmental conservation, highlighting the negative environmental impacts of mining. It does not suggest that economic development is inherently incompatible with environmental conservation, but rather that current policies often prioritize short-term economic gains over ecological preservation.

options.text: Rakesh is an excellent communicator.

options.text: Consumers prioritize essential goods over luxury items during an economic downturn.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a valid conclusion based on the information given?

options.text: John will certainly live longer than those who do not exercise.
options.explanation: The passage does not support a definitive conclusion about John's life expectancy compared to others.

options.text: John's cardiovascular health is likely improved due to exercise.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical deduction from the given premises.

options.explanation: The passage does not imply that exercise is the only way to achieve improved cardiovascular health.

options.text: A longer life expectancy is guaranteed for those who exercise regularly.
options.explanation: The passage suggests a general trend, not a guarantee.

questions.question: Which of the following statements can be logically deduced from the given information?

options.text: All fruits are naturally grown.
options.explanation: This option makes an unwarranted connection that cannot be deduced.

options.text: Some naturally grown things are fruits.
options.explanation: This option makes an unwarranted connection that cannot be deduced.

options.text: All sweet things are fruits.
options.explanation: This option makes an unwarranted universal claim that cannot be deduced.

options.text: Some sweet things are not fruits.
options.explanation: This is a direct deduction from the fact that 'All fruits are sweet' implies that the set of 'sweet things' is larger than or equal to the set of 'fruits,' thus allowing for 'some sweet things' to be outside the 'fruits' category.

questions.explanation: The first statement tells us that the set of 'fruits' is a subset of 'sweet things.' The second statement tells us there's an overlap between 'sweet things' and 'naturally grown things,' but it doesn't specify if this overlap includes fruits.
questions.subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: What can be logically concluded about Rohan based on the information above?

options.text: Rohan does not own a car.
options.explanation: This option is a possibility but not a necessary conclusion based on the given statements.

options.text: Rohan is too young to drive.
options.explanation: This option is a possibility but not a necessary conclusion based on the given statements.

options.text: Rohan does not have a valid license.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical conclusion based on the application of Modus Tollens.

options.text: Rohan has a valid license but chooses not to drive.
options.explanation: This option is a possibility but not a necessary conclusion based on the given statements.

questions.explanation: This is an application of Modus Tollens. The first statement establishes a conditional relationship: (Valid License) → (Permitted to Drive). The second statement gives us the negation of the consequent: (Not Permitted to Drive). Therefore, we can logically deduce the negation of the antecedent: (Not Valid License).

questions.question: Which of the following is the most direct logical conclusion that can be drawn from the passage?

options.text: Most people are aware of the health risks of processed foods.
options.explanation: This option is an assumption and cannot be directly deduced from the passage.

options.text: The government should ban all processed foods.
options.explanation: This option is a policy recommendation and cannot be directly deduced from the passage.

options.text: A significant portion of the population is at risk of poor health outcomes due to diet.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical conclusion based on the information provided in the passage.

options.text: People who consume processed foods do not eat healthy foods.
options.explanation: This option is an overgeneralization and cannot be directly deduced from the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage states that excessive consumption of processed foods contributes to poor health outcomes and that a significant portion of the population regularly consumes processed foods. Combining these two facts directly leads to the conclusion that a significant portion of the population is at risk of poor health outcomes because of this dietary habit.

questions.question: Based on the statements, which of the following must be true?

options.text: Company Y is a successful business.
options.explanation: This option cannot be deduced because prioritizing customer satisfaction is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one, for success.

options.text: Company X will eventually prioritize customer satisfaction.
options.explanation: This option is a speculation and cannot be deduced from the given statements.

options.text: Company X is not a successful business.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical conclusion based on the application of Modus Tollens.

options.text: Company Y is more successful than Company X.
options.explanation: This option cannot be deduced because prioritizing customer satisfaction is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one, for success.

questions.explanation: The first statement establishes a necessary condition for success: (Successful Business) → (Prioritizes Customer Satisfaction). The second statement tells us that Company X does not meet this necessary condition (Not Prioritizes Customer Satisfaction). Therefore, by Modus Tollens, Company X cannot be a successful business.

questions.question: Which of the following is an underlying assumption required for the conclusion to be logically valid?

options.text: Controlling inflation is the only factor for economic stability.
options.explanation: This option is too strong; the passage says it must control inflation, not that it's the only factor.

options.text: The government has the sole responsibility for controlling inflation.
options.explanation: This option is about responsibility, not the logical connection between inflation and stability.

options.text: High inflation directly threatens economic stability.
options.explanation: This is an underlying assumption required for the conclusion to be logically valid.

options.text: The government has the means to control inflation effectively.
options.explanation: This option is about capability, not the logical link.

questions.explanation: The argument states: (Government must control inflation for stability) + (High inflation exists, meaning government hasn't controlled it) → (Economic stability is at risk). For this conclusion to follow, there must be a direct link between 'high inflation' and 'economic stability being at risk.'
questions.subject: upsc-csat

questions.question: The reasoning in the argument above is flawed because it:

options.text: Relies on an unproven generalization.
options.explanation: This option does not directly address the flaw in the reasoning.

options.text: Confuses correlation with causation.
options.explanation: This option does not apply to the given argument.

options.text: Does not provide sufficient evidence for the first premise.
options.explanation: This option does not directly address the flaw in the reasoning.

options.text: Uses a false premise in a logically valid structure.
options.explanation: The flaw is in the truthfulness of a key premise, not in the structure of the deduction itself.

questions.explanation: The structure of the argument (All A are B, C is A, Therefore C is B) is a classic valid syllogism (Barbara). If the premises were true, the conclusion would necessarily follow. However, the first premise, 'All birds can fly,' is factually false.

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions can be most logically drawn from the passage?

options.text: Consuming fewer than five servings of fruits and vegetables daily guarantees chronic diseases.
options.explanation: This option is an extreme and unwarranted generalization.

options.text: All individuals who consume five servings of fruits and vegetables daily will never get chronic diseases.
options.explanation: This option is an extreme and unwarranted generalization.

options.text: Increasing fruit and vegetable intake to five servings daily can contribute to better health.
options.explanation: This is a cautious and logical deduction based on the correlation found in the study and the expert recommendation.

options.text: Dietary intake is the sole determinant of chronic disease incidence.
options.explanation: This option is an oversimplification; the passage does not claim diet is the sole determinant.

questions.explanation: The study found a lower incidence of chronic diseases with higher intake of fruits and vegetables, and experts recommend meeting this dietary guideline.

questions.question: Which of the following must be true based on the given statements?

options.text: All children using the pool are members of the club.
options.explanation: This option is not necessarily true; the statement only mentions 'some children' using the pool.

options.text: All members of the club are children.
options.explanation: This option is not necessarily true; the statement does not provide information about all members.

options.text: Some children are members of the club.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical conclusion based on the given statements.

options.text: Some members of the club are using the swimming pool.
options.explanation: This is a direct logical conclusion based on the given statements.

questions.explanation: The first statement means (Using Pool) → (Member of Club). The second statement tells us that 'Some children are using the swimming pool.' If some children are using the pool, and only members are allowed to use the pool, then those specific children must be members.
